subject: Production timeouts & client retry loop - urgent investigation
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finstream.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Li <ben.li@finstream.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production timeouts / 429 spike - urgent

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a large spike of 5xx/429s and downstream timeouts hitting our Redwood routes this morning around 08:45 PT. Our frontend experienced cascading timeouts — user-facing latency jumped from ~200ms to 3–7s and a subset of requests now consistently return 502/503/429.

Attached is a short screenshot and a trimmed trace bundle (request-trace-sample.log). We rolled a release earlier this week but rolled it back at 07:30 after the initial uptick; however, traffic patterns show continued retry bursts even after the rollback.

Can Redwood please:
- Confirm whether there's any service-side throttle or capacity issue for our account (FinStream, acct id 8412).
- Provide a short-term mitigation (per-customer rate limit or circuit-breaker) while we investigate client-side behavior.
- Let us know any recommended SDK settings we should enforce on our side.

This is impacting payments flows for some customers and we need a fast path.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform — FinStream
elena.morales@finstream.com

Team — looping you in for immediate triage. Summary: FinStream is seeing elevated 5xx/429 rates + timeouts; they report continued retry bursts after a rollback. Attached trace points to repeated identical request patterns originating from the customer IP pool.

Initial ask:
- Rafael / Dylan: can you confirm whether this looks like a client-side retry storm (synchronized retries) vs. a service degradation? Check upstream request headers (X-Redwood-Request-Id, user-agent/SDK-version) and any sudden concurrency bursts.
- Grace: please open an internal throttle rule (per-customer) we can toggle while we triage.

I created INF-7123 and uploaded the customer's trace. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7123

Stephanie Nguyen

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Elena Morales <elena.morales@finstream.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production timeouts / 429 spike - urgent — quick triage

Stephanie / team — quick findings from an initial log sweep:

- Evidence of a retry storm: many request traces show the same client request repeated ~8–12 times within 90s windows from the same client IP ranges. The timestamps line up with our 429s (service responded -> client retried immediately -> more 429s).
- Important identifier: the user-agent identifies the call as "finstream-sdk/1.4.0" and there's no jitter in backoff; retries are essentially immediate.
- Server side: capacity looks healthy for the route, but we see transient queueing on a small pool of instances that pushed up latency and triggered more client retries. In short: a client-driven retry amplification.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can be applied server-side within minutes):
1) Enable a soft per-account rate limit at the edge for FinStream to dampen bursts (temporary, adjustable).
2) Enforce "Retry-After" and honor client-specified backoff headers; return 429 with Retry-After when threshold reached to avoid 503 cascades.
3) Apply connection/concurrency caps per source IP range.

Customer fix recommendations (for FinStream):
- Upgrade finstream-sdk to 2.1.3 (includes exponential backoff + jitter by default).
- Set max_retries=4, base_backoff_ms=200, jitter=true, and enable idempotency keys where applicable.

I've attached the short playbook we used for similar incidents (redwood-troubleshoot-playbook.md) and linked INF-7123. If folks approve I'll push the per-account limit now.

Rafael Mendes
SRE — Redwood Inference

A few updates from our side: we rolled back the client release and disabled the new retry helper yesterday, but we still see a tail of older clients (mobile app versions ~v1.3.x) that don't have the patched SDK. Those clients are still generating retry bursts. We've attached an expanded trace with client IP ranges.

Two asks:

- We will need an assessment for potential SLA credit; this materially affected card-payment success rates for ~40 minutes.

Elena

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finstream.com>, Ben Li <ben.li@finstream.com>, ceo@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production timeouts / 429 spike - urgent — exec summary & next steps

TL;DR: Root cause = retry amplification from older FinStream SDK clients (no jitter, aggressive immediate retries) causing transient queueing and elevated 5xx/429. We implemented a short-term server-side dampening and have a plan for remediation.

What we did (completed):
- Rolled a temporary per-account rate limit at the edge for FinStream (limits are configurable; currently set conservatively to avoid aborting legitimate traffic).
- Added a soft enforcement of Retry-After headers to reduce immediate retries turning into spikes.
- Increased instance concurrency bounds on the affected pool and enabled rapid autoscale triggers for the route.

Customer actions (in progress):
- FinStream is pushing a patch to the mobile fleet; they estimate ~70% of active clients will have the updated SDK within 48 hours.
- We recommended & documented recommended SDK settings (SDK v2.1.3 w/ exponential backoff + jitter, max_retries=4).

Next steps and asks (owners):
- Rafael: please prepare a short postmortem draft (INF-7123) with timeline, metrics (5xx/429 rate pre- and post-mitigation), and recommended long-term protections (circuit-breaker, per-account adaptive throttling). Target: publish by EOD 2026-10-07.
- Grace: coordinate billing team on preliminary SLA credit estimate; FinStream has requested early guidance.
- Dylan: prepare a short SDK compatibility note we can send to partners highlighting safe defaults and the risks of immediate retries.
- Stephanie (me): schedule a follow-up call with FinStream PM/Platform next 24 hours to review MAP and remediation steps.

Status: customer traffic has stabilized (5xx/429 reduced by ~85% after the edge limit), but we'll keep the temporary dampening in place until client patch uptake reaches a safe threshold.

Elena — please let me know if this summary matches your observations and if you want to schedule the exec call.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Lead, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
